description.from: The marketing site tells buyers the goal is a setting. Show what it does: rerun the first 400 cycles with selection primary set to precision, to F1, and to balanced Brier (the default), same seed and corpus, and record the three numbers plus calibration per window. Acceptance: a comparison table in the results note and, if the differences are clear, a fixture the site can show on the how-it-works page under the three goal cards. If the differences are within noise, say so and the site keeps its current wording.
description.to:
Ryan, 2026-10-09: over the long term we want to show examples that had different optimization priorities, one optimizing for precision and one for recall, and show how the accuracy, precision, and recall curves change differently for each. We hope to confirm that they do, and to see it visually. We are studying our own product. The result becomes a visualization on the marketing site.

Design: on the extended corpus, run the same seed and settings three or four times with the selection primary set to precision, recall, F1, and balanced Brier (the default). Record per-100-cycle windows: accuracy, precision, recall, F1, Brier, calibration error, stated confidence, optimizer events, and labels used. Hypotheses to test: (1) the precision run's precision climbs faster and higher while its recall falls or stalls; (2) the recall run does the opposite; (3) F1 lands between them; (4) accuracy differs less than precision and recall do; (5) calibration quality does not depend much on the goal. State each as a pre-registered expectation before running, and report where the data disagrees.

Output: a fixture with one curve per metric per goal, and a results note. Site: a how-it-works pictogram showing three curves per goal, drawn in the same visual language as the home page pictograms, with the glossary subtitles under each metric and marks rather than colour to tell runs apart. Only show it if the runs differ beyond noise; otherwise say so on the page.

Acceptance: recordings for each goal; a comparison table; the pre-registered hypotheses with pass or fail; and, if warranted, the fixture and pictogram on the site.
